info.title: Building Group 14 team website with AI perspectives

parts.text: Build our team website. Read all profiles in content/*.md (ignore _template.md). Images are in content/images/. Requirements: One standalone file site/index.html: HTML + CSS + JavaScript only, nothing loaded from the internet (no CDNs, no web fonts, no external images). Introduce the team (we are Group 14) and every member: photo, name, study background, interests, fun fact and hot take. A section "Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering" that combines what all five of us wrote: where we agree and where we differ. Use our own words and ideas, and don't invent facts about us. Responsive (phone ~375px and desktop), plus a day/night mode toggle. Funny and creative. Surprise us, but keep it readable. Images, important: do NOT write base64 yourself. Write the page source to site/index.src.html using placeholders like , then generate the final file with uv run python embed_images.py site/index.src.html --images content/images --out site/index.html. Never open or read site/index.html (it contains huge base64 data). Always edit index.src.html and regenerate. Then check it with uv run python check_site.py site/index.html --content content and fix things until all checks pass. First tell me your plan and design idea briefly, then build it.

**Plan:** I’ll read each member profile (excluding `_template.md`) and check the image filenames and site-check requirements. Then I’ll create a single self-contained, responsive Group 14 page with a playful “team field guide” design, member cards, a synthesis of your shared and differing views on AI, and a day/night toggle. I’ll use image placeholders in `site/index.src.html`, generate `site/index.html` with the provided script, and run the checker.

display.text:
# Shrividya

## Study background

Currently pursuing an M.Sc. in Computer Science at Paderborn University, Germany. Previously completed a B.E. in Information Science and Engineering from Global Academy of Technology, Bengaluru, India.  I also have experience interning with cybersecurity companies, gaining hands-on exposure to cloud security, DevSecOps and security automation.

## Interests

Sketching, playing basketball, dancing, exploring new places, discovering different cultures and trying out new technologies.

## Fun fact

Basketball is where I learned that teamwork matters, even when nobody wants to pass the ball.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI has made software development faster and easier, but it hasn't made developers less responsible. It can help us write code, find bugs and solve problems, but it can also make mistakes that are easy to miss. I think AI is a great teammate, as long as we don't let it do all the thinking for us.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I think AI agents will become a normal part of software development. They will be able to handle bigger tasks, from writing code to testing and fixing bugs. Developers will spend more time planning, making decisions and checking the results. But understanding the basics will always matter, because someone still needs to know when the AI gets things wrong.

## My hot take on AI

AI can write the code, but it cannot take responsibility when the system breaks at 3 AM!
